workflows.description: Canonical reusable workflow for a broad, multi-source entity profile or an explicit comparison of asserted facts with uncertain or proposed relationships. It reconciles focal-concept facts, text, predicate incidence, grounded relations, and uncertainty-bearing assertions.
workflows.content: Resolve the target entity from authenticated or explicit context and use this workflow when the requested work product needs a multi-faceted profile, cross-checking across distinct evidence surfaces, or an explicit separation of asserted facts from uncertain or proposed relationships. For a single bounded fact or relation extent, prefer an adequate direct read or small composition. Retrieve and reconcile the workflow's required evidence, then answer directly from grounded represented evidence and preserve any material gap.

input_mappings.description: Pass through the user's entity-information request.

selection_profile.description: Select predicates that retrieve scholarly-work extents for an entity-information request whose expected-outcome contract names a scholarly target type.

llm_policy.response_contract_text: Answer the user directly from grounded represented evidence. For broad self-profile, represented-self, authorship, ownership, affiliation, role, and other entity-relative relation questions, first fetch the focal entity concept, inspect predicate incidence with argument type counts in every relation direction, retrieve narrowed relation evidence, and check uncertainty-bearing relationship assertions for the same focal entity. When the user asks to separate established facts from likely inferences, report asserted relation/focal-concept evidence separately from uncertain or proposed relationship assertions; do not merge those categories. Once the five required evidence tools have succeeded and the relation result contains the requested related entity IDs, names, and applicable type evidence, answer immediately from those results. When Vontology expands an observed predicate through represented inverse or relation-family metadata, use every returned family predicate rather than reporting only the initially observed predicate. Do not fetch or summarise predicate concepts merely to restate a predicate label or description already present in the incidence and relation evidence. If a required evidence call fails or lacks a necessary field, preserve that typed failure so the outer represented recovery policy can choose a retry, alternate extent, or narrower answer instead of spending successful-path calls on speculative re-reading. For every predicate-filtered entity-relative request, once incidence or represented predicate-family expansion identifies matching predicates, the content-bearing read must use find_relations_with_argument with those exact predicates in predicate_filter; an unfiltered relation page is not evidence for a matching row that falls outside the returned page. predicate_filter, argument_index, relation_kind, and relation paging limits belong to find_relations_with_argument, not fetch_concept. Never send relation-query arguments to fetch_concept, and never answer a relation-extent request from such a fetch because it does not perform the required filtered relation read. If an earlier relation read was unfiltered or omitted the matching row, call find_relations_with_argument again with the narrowed predicate_filter before answering. For papers, inspect predicate incidence before relation paging, then filter the resulting extent by the requested type before answering. If predicate incidence for a paper request exposes #V#author_of or #V#owner_of with paper-like type counts or sample groundings, the next relation lookup must use find_relations_with_argument with a predicate_filter containing those exact predicate IDs; do not use an unfiltered relation page first. If predicate incidence exposes role-expansion summaries for reified/event/claim neighbours, use role-filler type counts to choose the follow-up extent and do not treat the reified neighbour itself as the answer entity. Do not claim that no matching results exist unless the relation-bearing and uncertainty-bearing evidence in this turn supports that negative conclusion. If grounded evidence is insufficient, say that clearly instead of guessing. When using relation hits, use each hit's related_concept_id, related_name, related_type_ids, and direction_from_focal_entity fields; these fields resolve whether the related entity is the source or target, and duplicate relations for the same neighbour are compacted. Include every unique related entity whose related_type_ids establish the requested result class, regardless of whether the relation predicate is outgoing or incoming. Emit every relation-grounded result as a Markdown bullet with a resolved `#V#...` concept ID wherever that relation-hit concept ID is available. Never emit relation-grounded results as bare assertion syntax such as `subject --predicate--> object`. If a related concept ID is missing, do not fabricate one: omit that item from the list and state clearly that no usable `#V#` ID was returned. Use a single-item bullet if only one grounded entity is returned. Relation-grounded outputs must be bullet entries with the resolved `#V#` ID token for navigation.

context_fields.label: Historical successful-run guidance: soft hints from prior successful executions.
Historical failure-avoidance guidance: past failure patterns to avoid when relevant.
Low-imposition exploration guidance: optional next-run probe; do not slow the user down or ask unnecessary questions to satisfy it.
